retained_changes.linux_socket_buffer_display: Linux ss rb/tb values include the kernel buffer accounting multiplier; sysctl ceilings are 7 MiB each.

decision: Retain larger UDP buffer ceilings: measured reception overflow disappeared at comparable traffic volumes. Do not add fixed limits or replace the existing queue without evidence of harmful queuing.
latency_result: No proven reduction of idle network or HTTPS latency. Warmed first response increased from 435.514 to 509.111 ms in this pair; path and destination were not pinned and the sessions were not concurrent.
limitations: Single sequential before/after pair; changing WAN conditions and other user traffic were not isolated.
Sixteen 8 MiB requests per direction include setup overhead and gaps; the result is not a long-running saturated bandwidth guarantee.
The warm measurement uses new curl HTTPS requests; it does not prove uninterrupted QUIC session reuse or measure a complete web page.
Global UDP counters cover all services; the baseline UDP443 socket drop counter also rose by 321 in the upload window.
The normal lifecycle final sample precedes service restart by a short interval; bytes produced in that interval may not be recorded.
browser_action: The panel worker restarted; sign in again if the browser session expired. Client profile re-download is unnecessary.
maintenance_note: The first run used an incorrect backend readiness path and restored the original ceilings and services. The corrected readiness check and final apply passed.
